chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who raised it from Abi Maryam, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought al-Najashi the poet, who had drunk wine in the month of Ramadan. So he flogged him with eighty lashes, then imprisoned him for a night. Then he called for him the next day and flogged him with twenty lashes. He said to him, “O Amir al-Mu'minin, these eighty lashes you gave me were for drinking wine, but what are these twenty?” He said, “This is for your audacity in drinking wine in the month of Ramadan.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine; an intoxicating drink whose consumption is forbidden
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes, the hadd punishment mentioned here for drinking wine
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting
key_terms.عِشْرِينَ سَوْطًا: twenty lashes, an additional disciplinary punishment
key_terms.لِتَجَرِّئِكَ: for your audacity or boldness in committing the act

ai.seo_question: What punishment did Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام give for drinking wine in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام punished a man for drinking wine during Ramadan. It indicates both the prescribed hadd for drinking intoxicants and an additional disciplinary punishment due to violating the sanctity of the month of Ramadan.
